findings.body: Raise: Functional. Handback records the worker question locally but never refreshes an existing pull request. The kit path refreshes the PR after a question in `src/forge/worker.py:325`. If a native round asks a question after publication, collaborators reading the PR see stale history until a later command refreshes it.
findings.title: Published pull requests miss native worker questions

findings.body: Raise: Test. The named command proof sets `repo = "forge-source"` and exercises only a fresh checkout. The adopted-repo role and guide tests never run client `forge work` through `forge handback`. Native routing, restoration, and landing could break in a new or earlier-adopted client while this proof passes, contrary to the repository's client-coverage rule.
findings.title: Not done: native work in new and earlier-adopted client repos

findings.body: Raise: Test. This test reads the whole brief but never the short brief, checks `forge next` but not the running board, and supplies only trusted Codex settings and nonempty handbacks. It also commits before the second handback. It would therefore pass if the short brief were missing, the board omitted the round, native Codex skipped its trust check, empty stdin failed to record a failed round, or a second handback with leftover changes omitted its warning. Done-when 3 names each behavior.
findings.title: Not done: native work's named handout and failure outcomes have proof
